skill.name: diagnosing-superpowers
skill.description: Analyze coding-agent session transcripts to explain delays, repeated work, plan drift, failures, and unsupported claims with cited evidence.
skill.summary: Build evidence-based session diagnostics and privacy-reviewed bug reports.
skill.author: obra

content.value_statement: Coding-agent sessions can waste time without showing where behavior diverged. This skill analyzes transcripts and produces cited reports for review or issue filing.
actual_capabilities: Locates and verifies current or historical session transcripts.
Builds a cited timeline of prompts, skills, tools, errors, and subagents.
Checks plan adherence, repeated work, stumbles, quality evidence, conflicts, cost, and time.
Measures transcript files before reading and limits extracted content.
Creates structured diagnosis reports with path and line citations.
Prepares user-approved, redacted bundles and GitHub issue drafts.
limitations: Requires accessible session transcripts and enough metadata to identify the correct session.
Reports evidence but does not identify defects or recommend Superpowers changes.
Cannot guarantee that automated redaction catches every sensitive value.
Creates archives or GitHub issues only after explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Explain Unexpected Agent Work
use_cases.description: Trace repeated commands, plan drift, errors, and unsupported completion claims in one coding session.

use_cases.title: Analyze Cost and Delay
use_cases.description: Measure supported token use, long turns, idle gaps, large tool results, and subagent activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Maintainer Report
use_cases.description: Create a cited report, search related issues, and prepare a scrubbed bundle after approval.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose One Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this session: [session ID or path]. I expected [result], but observed [problem]. Focus on [observable].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a scoped diagnosis with known session details.

prompt_templates.title: Find Repeated Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [session] for repeated reads, edits, commands, searches, or decisions. Explain what changed between repetitions and cite every finding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate duplicated work in a coding-agent session.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Time and Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [session] for supported token use, longest turns, idle gaps, large tool results, compactions, and associated-session costs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Explain why a session was slow or expensive.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scrubbed Bug Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Superpowers bug report for [session]. Search related issues, draft exact text, and offer a redacted evidence bundle for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced maintainer-ready report with privacy controls.

output_examples.input: Why did session abc123 repeat the same file reads?
output_examples.output: A repeated-work report listing grouped reads, intervening changes, turn ranges, evidence lines, and confidence for each finding.

output_examples.input: Why was this session expensive and slow?
output_examples.output: A cost summary covering supported token totals, longest turns, idle gaps, large tool results, compactions, and associated sessions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a report for the Superpowers maintainers.
output_examples.output: A cited diagnosis, related-issue results, an approved issue draft, and an optional scrubbed bundle with privacy limitations.

best_practices: Provide the session identifier, expected result, observed problem, and observable that matters.
Review every citation and redacted file before sharing a bundle.
Approve exact issue text and archive contents only after checking the scrub log.
anti_patterns: Do not request an unscoped sweep when one event or turn range matters.
Do not treat current files or versions as proof of historical session state.
Do not publish transcript bundles without independent review and explicit approval.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose a past session?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a session identifier or path, and confirm the first prompt and timestamp when asked.

faq.question: Does it modify session transcripts?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires read-only handling of source session files.

faq.question: What evidence does the report include?
faq.answer: Each finding includes a source path, line number, short quotation, turn range, and confidence.

faq.question: Can it explain token cost and elapsed time?
faq.answer: Yes, when transcripts contain supported usage counters, timestamps, event boundaries, and documented units.

faq.question: Will it create a GitHub issue automatically?
faq.answer: No. It shows the exact issue text and creates the issue only after explicit approval.

faq.question: Are exported bundles guaranteed to contain no secrets?
faq.answer: No. The workflow scrubs and audits bundles, but users must review every file before sharing.
